To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) linear threshold networks with lateral inhibition can be designed to group arbitrary sets of neurons, (b) the grouping can be achieved in an information-preserving way, and (c) the optimal sparsity for the groups is unphysiological for dense inputs but more plausible for sparse inputs.

a linear threshold network can be organized to have lateral inhibition such that any permitted group of neurons that can coactivate in a stable steady state must belong to one of the preselected groups.

a linear-threshold network with lateral inhibition and a collection of overlapping groups can be used to implement a winner-take-all network, and that the optimal sparsity in such a network is unphysiologic for dense inputs but more plausible when the groups and the input are equally sparse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of selectively grouping neurons in networks of lateral inhibition, a process that has been hypothesized to be important in many cognitive tasks.
a fundamental question of how a network can perform a grouping operation on a set of arbitrary groups.
the problem of how the brain might group neurons to form a winner-take-all network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work provides a theoretical framework for the analysis and design of winner-take-all networks with arbitrary group structures.
we show that the winner-take-all network can be extended to a more general network that groups neurons in a selective fashion.
we have shown how to group arbitrary sets of neurons into permitted groups in linear threshold networks of lateral inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a new model that can be used to study the dynamics of a network that is composed of a mixture of discrete (e.g. binary) neurons and continuous (e.g. graded response) ones, and have shown that the dynamics of the discrete neurons can be described by a winner-take-all mechanism.
we have developed a new model of a recurrent network that can be used to group neurons based on the input.

we show that a linear threshold network with a particular lateral inhibition can be viewed as a Winner-Take-All network with a particular grouping of the neurons, and that the grouping can be arbitrary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple linear threshold network with lateral inhibition can be used to implement winner-take-all networks with arbitrary groupings of neurons.
lateral inhibition can be used to group the activity of arbitrary sets of neurons in a network.
the grouping of neurons in winner-take-all networks can be controlled by lateral inhibition.
